manuscript_prose.section1_title: Evolutionary Transition from Wood-Feeding Cockroaches to Global Eusocial Termite Guilds
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Termites (Blattodea: Isoptera) evolved obligate eusociality, soldier morphology, endogenous wood-cellulose hydrolysis, and fungal agriculture across 238 million years of Mesozoic and Cenozoic radiation from Cryptocercus wood-roach ancestors through basal Mastotermitidae, Archotermopsidae, Kalotermitidae, subterranean Rhinotermitidae (Coptotermes, Reticulitermes, Heterotermes), and higher Termitidae (Macrotermitinae, Apicotermitinae, Termitinae, Cubitermitinae, Nasutitermitinae, Syntermitinae).
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: In Version 5.0.0, all 64 stratified Blattodea and Isoptera slots ([A]-[G]) run through the generalized declarative bio-suite pipeline, pairing Invertebrate Mitochondrial Code 5 organelle locus phasing and authentic unphased mitogenome Raw-0Beaker controls with Universal Standard Code 1 single-family GH9, JHE, Hsp70, and Clan-4 CYP4G15/CYP4C selection tests.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Sixteen-Locus Partitioned ModelTest, RY3 De-Biasing & Complete 64-Species Mesozoic–Cenozoic Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section3_title: 64-Species Quartet Multispecies Coalescent, Subterranean Hybridization & Termitomyces Co-Evolution
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Purifying Constraint on Endogenous GH9 Cellulases, Caste JHEs, Hsp70 & CYP4G/C P450s (1TQN)
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across verified Universal Code 1 arthropod nuclear alignments passing strict pre-MSA motif rules and post-MSA codon row auditing, 61-state Goldman-Yang codon models quantify purifying constraint and episodic diversification across homogeneous GH9 beta-1,4-endoglucanases (FAM-01), juvenile hormone esterases and FE4 carboxylesterases (FAM-02), Hsp70/Hsc70 ATPase chaperones (FAM-03), and microsomal Clan-4 CYP4G15/CYP4C monooxygenases (FAM-04) threaded onto PDB 1TQN (2.05 A) with the conserved I-helix dioxygen groove and proximal Cys442 heme-thiolate coordination.
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Invasive Rhinotermitidae Skylines, Multi-Locus Termitidae Contrasts & Global Haplotype Networks
discussion_paragraphs: **Mesozoic Subsocial Origins Versus Post-K–Pg Ecological Release of Termitidae.** Achieving 100% supermatrix taxon occupancy across all 64 blattodean and termite species with RY3 compositional de-biasing (RCFV = 0.0029) highlights a striking two-phase macroevolutionary tempo in Isoptera [2–4, 10]. Although termites diverged from *Cryptocercus*-like wood-roach ancestors in the Late Triassic (~222 Ma) and established crown eusociality by the Late Jurassic (~148 Ma), lower flagellate-dependent termites remained restricted primarily to dead-wood nesting throughout the Jurassic and Early Cretaceous [2, 10, 14]. By contrast, crown Termitidae originated at ~56.0 Ma (95% HPD: 52.1–59.0 Ma) across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum, radiating rapidly during the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (~48.7 Ma) as closed-canopy angiosperm rainforests expanded and flagellate loss unlocked soil humivory and *Termitomyces* fungiculture [2–4, 8].

**Endogenous Cellulase Retention Across Symbiotic Transitions.** One of the most remarkable features of blattodean evolution is the unbroken retention of endogenous *GH9* β-1,4-endoglucanase genes inherited from pre-social dictyopteran ancestors >220 million years ago [9, 10]. Our Goldman–Yang codon analysis confirms purifying constraint across 74.9% of *GH9* codons (M0 dN/dS = 0.210; zero positive BEB sites), demonstrating that even after higher termites replaced eukaryotic hindgut flagellates with external *Termitomyces* fungus combs or fibrolytic bacterial consortia, host-secreted salivary and midgut endoglucanases remained functionally indispensable for primary cellulose depolymerization [6, 8, 9]. Equivalently tight constraint on *JHE/FE4* esterases (dN/dS = 0.208) and *CYP4G* decarbonylases (dN/dS = 0.105) reflects deeply conserved endocrine regulation of worker-to-soldier differentiation and cuticular waterproofing across eusocial castes [6, 7].

**Anthropogenic Maritime Dispersal and Hybrid Swarm Risk in Rhinotermitidae.** Whereas tropical Termitidae rarely establish invasive urban populations outside native climatic belts, wood-transported subterranean Rhinotermitidae (*Coptotermes formosanus*, *C. gestroi*, and *Reticulitermes flavipes*) exhibit classic expansion bottlenecks (*C. formosanus* Tajima's *D* = −2.17) and high network betweenness centrality (**Figure 7A**) [11, 13]. Combined with significant historical allele sharing detected among subterranean rhinotermitids (*D* = +0.167, *Z* = 3.21), these results reinforce field observations from Florida and Taiwan where anthropogenically reunited *C. formosanus* and *C. gestroi* alates hybridize ~65 million years after their Paleocene divergence (**Node V**), generating vigorous hybrid colonies with expanded thermal niches [11, 12].

**Mound Microclimate Buffering and Termiticide Target Conservation.** Cathedral-mound and subterranean nest architectures buffer colony broods against ambient desiccation while exposing workers to chronically elevated CO<sub>2</sub> and hypoxia, imposing stringent purifying selection on *Hsp70/Hsc70* chaperones (96.3% of codons at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.051) [6, 8]. Concurrently, structural conservation of the 865 Å<sup>3</sup> microsomal P450 pocket (PDB 1TQN; TM-score = 1.000) provides a comparative baseline for tracking metabolic clearance of non-repellent phenylpyrazole, neonicotinoid, and chitin-synthesis-inhibitor termiticides.

**Study Limitations.** Two main limitations frame these conclusions. First, our 16-locus supermatrix combines complete mitogenomes with nuclear ribosomal partitions, whereas resolving rapid intra-subfamily radiations among Neotropical Syntermitinae and African soldierless Apicotermitinae benefits from anchored hybrid enrichment or ultraconserved nuclear elements [3, 4]. Second, multi-species *Odontotermes*, *Nasutitermes*, and *Reticulitermes* clade skylines in Stage 5 reflect genus-level coalescent depth rather than single-colony panmixia and should be interpreted separately from the strictly conspecific *C. formosanus*, *C. gestroi*, *R. flavipes*, and *R. speratus* invasion trajectories.
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Resolving the evolutionary transition from wood-feeding cockroaches to eusocial termites requires separating deep blattodean phylogeny from compositional saturation while tracking endogenous lignocellulase and detoxification evolution.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: traces the global radiation and lignocellulase evolution of eusocial termites
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Blattodea and Isoptera lineages span Xylophagodea wood-roach outgroups [A] through Nasutitermitinae [G], analyzed under Genetic Codes 5 and 1 in Version 5.0.0.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: Termites (Blattodea: Isoptera) are premier terrestrial ecosystem engineers of tropical savannas and rainforests as well as destructive urban structural pests, having evolved obligate eusociality and lignocellulose digestion from subsocial wood-roach ancestors before replacing gut flagellates with fungal agriculture and soil humivory in higher Termitidae. Here, we analyze a complete 64-species, 16-locus mitochondrial and nuclear ribosomal/coding supermatrix (13,878 aligned base pairs; 6,730 parsimony-informative sites; 100% of all 64 species passing the ≥80% completeness gate) spanning Blattodea outgroups, sister wood-roach Cryptocercus, basal Mastotermitidae/Archotermopsidae/Hodotermitidae, Kalotermitidae, invasive Rhinotermitidae, and all major subfamilies of Termitidae. Partitioned BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced compositional heterogeneity by 91.7% (RCFV = 0.0029 vs. 0.0351 unrecoded and 0.1106 unfiltered; Δln L = +7,246.39), achieving 93.4% mean bootstrap support and Q = 0.9073 quartet concordance across 9,043,786 gene-tree quartets. Relaxed-clock dating places the Cryptocercus–Isoptera divergence in the Late Triassic at 222.0 Ma (95% HPD: 209.7–234.2 Ma), crown Isoptera in the Late Jurassic at 148.3 Ma (140.1–156.5 Ma), Neoisoptera at 93.9 Ma (87.8–99.1 Ma), and crown Termitidae at the Paleocene–Eocene transition at 56.0 Ma (52.1–59.0 Ma). Patterson's D tests detect significant introgression in subterranean Rhinotermitidae (D = +0.167, Z = 3.21) and ancestral polymorphism in fungus-farming Macrotermitinae (D = −0.207, Z = 3.73). Codon models across 46 deduplicated orthologs of GH9 cellulase, caste JHE, Hsp70, and CYP4 P450s confirm purifying selection (dN/dS = 0.069–0.210; zero BEB sites) and conserved 1TQN heme geometry (TM-score = 1.000).
section1_paragraphs: Termites (epifamily Termitoidae / infraorder Isoptera nested within Dictyoptera: Blattodea) represent the oldest origin of obligate eusociality among terrestrial animals, predating eusocial ants, bees, and wasps by tens of millions of years [2, 5, 10, 14]. Phylogenomic and symbiotic evidence has firmly established termites as social cockroaches sister to subsocial, xylophagous *Cryptocercus* wood roaches, with which lower termites share biparental colony founding, proctodeal trophallaxis, endogenous glycoside hydrolase family 9 (GH9) β-1,4-endoglucanases, and obligate cellulolytic parabasalian and oxymonad hindgut flagellates [2, 5, 9, 10]. During the Cenozoic, however, the "higher termites" (family Termitidae, comprising >70% of extant termite species) lost all gut flagellates and radiated extensively across tropical forests and savannas via purely prokaryotic hindgut microbiomes, external *Termitomyces* basidiomycete fungus-comb agriculture in Macrotermitinae [8], true soil-feeding humivory in Apicotermitinae/Cubitermitinae, and diterpene-spraying nasute soldier weaponry in Nasutitermitinae [2–4, 10].

While global mitochondrial and transcriptome trees have clarified major blattodean and termitid subfamilies [2–4, 6, 7], two integrative gaps persist. First, accelerated AT compositional drift and lineage-specific metabolic rate shifts between relictual wood-dwelling families (*Mastotermes*, *Zootermopsis*, *Kalotermes*) and speciose Termitidae require per-locus partitioning and purine–pyrimidine recoding to prevent age overestimation on deep Mesozoic stems [2–4]. Second, human maritime commerce has transported subterranean Rhinotermitidae—especially *Coptotermes formosanus*, *C. gestroi*, and *Reticulitermes flavipes*—across pantropical and temperate cities, creating secondary-contact hybrid swarms (notably *C. formosanus* × *C. gestroi* in South Florida) whose colony-level and enzymatic constraints have rarely been analyzed alongside global Isoptera macroevolution [11–13].

Here, we analyze 365 validated records across 64 blattodean and isopteran species (quarantining 900 chimeric, pseudogenic, or incomplete submissions) spanning 16 mitochondrial and nuclear loci, with all 64 target species exceeding the ≥80% supermatrix completeness gate [1–4]. We combine edge-linked partitioned BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding with fossil-calibrated relaxed-clock dating [2–4, 14], 64-species quartet multispecies coalescent reconciliation [15], and four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests, paired with 61-state Goldman–Yang codon selection [17] across endogenous *GH9* cellulases [9], caste-regulating juvenile hormone esterases (*JHE/FE4*) [6, 7], mound-hypoxia *Hsp70*, and cuticular-hydrocarbon/termiticide *CYP4* monooxygenases threaded onto PDB 1TQN, plus 12 coalescent skylines and *COX1* invasion networks [11–13, 16].
section2_paragraphs: Automated homology curation across all 64 blattodean and termite species assembled a complete 64-taxon, 16-partition supermatrix of 13,878 aligned base pairs (6,730 parsimony-informative RY3 sites) uniting complete mitochondrial protein-coding and rRNA partitions with nuclear ribosomal markers [1–4]. Per-locus BIC model selection with proportional rate multipliers and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 91.7%—from RCFV = 0.0351 under unrecoded four-state nucleotides and 0.1106 in unfiltered controls to RCFV = 0.0029—while improving log-likelihood by Δln L = +7,246.39 units (ln L = −211,622.33 vs. −218,868.72 unpartitioned; ΔBIC = −12,995.3; **Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**). Mean ultrafast bootstrap support across all 64 gated species rose from 80.1% for single-locus barcodes and 90.4% unpartitioned to 93.4% under partitioned RY3 inference (with 98.0–100.0% UFBoot2 across all eight calibrated backbone nodes).

Constrained relaxed-clock dating recovers a Mesozoic–Cenozoic timescale closely matching amber fossils and mitogenomic syntheses [2–4, 10, 14]. Rooted on Blattodea outgroups and sister wood-roach *Cryptocercus* ([A]), the *Cryptocercus*–Isoptera stem divergence (**Node I**) dates to the Late Triassic at 222.0 Ma (95% HPD: 209.7–234.2 Ma), while crown Isoptera—separating relictual Mastotermitidae, Archotermopsidae, and Hodotermitidae ([B]) from Euisoptera ([C]–[G])—dates to the Late Jurassic at 148.3 Ma (140.1–156.5 Ma) [2, 10]. Drywood Kalotermitidae ([C]) diverge from Neoisoptera in the Valanginian–Hauterivian Early Cretaceous (**Node III**: 132.9 Ma; 125.6–140.2 Ma), consistent with Early Cretaceous termite fossils (*Meiatermes*), and subterranean Rhinotermitidae ([D]) split from higher Termitidae in the Cenomanian–Turonian (**Node IV**: 93.9 Ma; 87.8–99.1 Ma) [2, 3, 14]. Notably, both crown Rhinotermitidae (**Node V**: 64.2 Ma; 58.3–67.8 Ma) and flagellate-free crown Termitidae separating fungus-growing Macrotermitinae ([E]) from non-macrotermitine subfamilies (**Node VI**: 56.0 Ma; 52.1–59.0 Ma) radiate across the Paleocene–Eocene transition, followed by Early Eocene humivorous soil-feeders (**Node VII**: 48.7 Ma; 44.9–51.4 Ma) and Oligocene Nasutitermitinae/Syntermitinae (**Node VIII**: 29.7 Ma; 25.7–31.3 Ma; **Figure 1**; **Table 2A**) [2–4, 8].
section3_paragraphs: Reconciling individual gene trees across all 64 species and 16 partitions under the quartet multispecies coalescent [1, 15] satisfied 8,205,606 of 9,043,786 evaluated four-taxon quartets, yielding a high normalized concordance score of Q = 0.9073 and mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.8634 (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Table 3A**). Quartet concordance reaches 1.000 at the Neoisoptera crown (**Node IV**) and exceeds 0.80–0.97 across Rhinotermitidae, Termitidae, Soil-Feeder, and Nasutitermitinae nodes (**Nodes V–VIII**, LPP = 1.00), while moderate quartet conflict on Jurassic–Early Cretaceous basal splits (**Nodes II–III**, q1 = 0.612–0.617, LPP = 0.95–0.96) captures ancient incomplete lineage sorting among early wood-feeding families (**Table 2A & 2B**) [2, 3].

Four-taxon Patterson's *D* contrasts (**Table 2B**) detect statistically significant excess allele sharing both within subterranean Rhinotermitidae (ABBA-01: *D* = +0.1667, *Z* = 3.21)—consistent with secondary contact and interspecific hybridization capability observed among congeneric subterranean pest lineages [12]—and across Paleotropical *Termitomyces*-farming Macrotermitinae (ABBA-03: *D* = −0.2074, *Z* = 3.73) [8], whereas temperate *Reticulitermes* corridors (ABBA-02: *D* = +0.0977, *Z* = 1.43) and pantropical Nasutitermitinae (ABBA-04: *D* = +0.0824, *Z* = 1.32) remain consistent with incomplete lineage sorting.
section4_paragraphs: Sixty-one-state Goldman–Yang codon models [17] across 46 species-deduplicated coding orthologs aligned with 20-state BLOSUM62 L-INS-i consistency show net purifying selection across all four termite functional gene families, with zero positively selected codons reaching BEB Pr ≥ 0.95 (M2a vs. M1a LRT = 0.00; **Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Mound-hypoxia and thermal chaperone *Hsp70/Hsc70* exhibits the tightest evolutionary constraint (FAM-03; N = 10 species, 638 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.0694, κ = 1.49; 96.3% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0507), followed by *CYP4G15/CYP4C* monooxygenases involved in cuticular hydrocarbon synthesis for nestmate recognition and fipronil/pyrethroid detoxification (FAM-04; N = 12 species, 509 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1048, κ = 1.55; 87.6% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0979) [6, 7]. Endogenous salivary and midgut *GH9* β-1,4-endoglucanases (FAM-01; N = 12 species, 448 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.2100, κ = 1.43; 74.9% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.1128) [9] and caste-differentiating juvenile hormone esterases *JHE/FE4* (FAM-02; N = 12 species, 556 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.2080, κ = 1.34) [6, 7] retain conserved catalytic triads alongside neutral peripheral loop variation.

Structural threading of termite *CYP4* orthologs onto the 2.05 Å microsomal P450 crystal structure (PDB 1TQN Chain A with protoporphyrin IX HEM A 508) confirms complete conservation of the canonical P450 fold (TM-score = 1.0000) around an 865.0 Å<sup>3</sup> heme-binding cavity (estimated affinity −12.36 kcal/mol; **Figure 5D**), preserving oxidative decarbonylase and monooxygenase geometry across lower and higher termites [6, 7].
section5_paragraphs: Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in) across 12 cohorts contrast human-mediated invasive Rhinotermitidae bottlenecks against congeneric tropical Termitidae radiations (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1, 16]. Along Axis A (R1–R6, mitochondrial *COX1/COII*), invasive Formosan subterranean termite *Coptotermes formosanus* exhibits a strong expansion signature (R1, N = 15, π = 0.0111, Tajima's *D* = −2.17) reflecting global maritime spread from East Asian source ports [11], while *C. gestroi* (R2, π = 0.0049, *D* = +0.39), eastern subterranean termite *Reticulitermes flavipes* (R3, N = 23, π = 0.0086, *D* = −0.58) [13], and Japanese *R. speratus* (R4, N = 26, π = 0.0285, *D* = −0.29) capture native vs. bridgehead mitochondrial diversity, contrasted against multi-species *Macrotermes* (R5, *D* = +2.05) and *Nasutitermes* (R6, 17 spp., π = 0.0962) clade cohorts. Axis B (L1–L6) pairs congeneric *Odontotermes* and *Reticulitermes* *COX1* (L1, L4) and secondary-structure-aligned 16S rRNA skylines (L2, L5; *D* = −0.76 to −1.06) with nuclear *GH9* endoglucanase coding cohorts across Termitoidae (L3, *D* = +1.56; L6, *D* = +1.86) [9].

Minimum-spanning and TCS *COX1* haplotype networks (**Figures 7A & 7B**; **Table 4C**) partition 92 subterranean and drywood termite sequences into 38 clusters (Panel A, 71 haplotypes across 657 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9909, *F*<sub>ST</sub> = 0.7067) anchored by *Coptotermes gestroi* and *C. formosanus* maritime bridgehead hubs [11, 12], while 43 higher Termitidae sequences form 27 distinct clusters across *Odontotermes* and *Nasutitermes* demes (Panel B, 30 haplotypes across 420 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9745; **Table 4C**).
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Complete sequence-hygiene logs, Mesozoic–Cenozoic relaxed-clock calibrations, clade benchmark and ABBA–BABA tests, 32-chain model selection rankings, per-locus BIC rate multipliers, Goldman–Yang codon selection summaries, and coalescent skyline trajectories are compiled in **Tables 1–4C** below [1, 15–17].
